NADIA [SURNAME]
[EMAIL] | [PHONE]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Platform Engineer and platform team technical lead with experience mentoring engineers moving from backend development into SRE and evaluating service mesh technologies.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | [EMPLOYER] | [DATES]
- Serve as technical lead for the platform team, without line-management responsibility.
- Mentored three backend engineers into SRE roles.
- Evaluated Istio and Linkerd in 2023; neither was adopted or run in production.
- Use the Backstage catalog; plugins were built by another team.

SPEAKING
“SLOs that product managers care about” — UK DevOps meetup, 2024

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clean, concise and factually cautious, but it is far too brief to compete for this role. It establishes seniority, technical leadership, mentoring and communication through speaking, but provides no measurable infrastructure outcomes, production responsibilities, architecture work, tools, cloud environment, reliability practices or security experience. The placeholders for the surname, email, phone, employer and dates make the document appear unfinished and are a significant professionalism issue. The distinction between technical leadership and line management is clear and appropriately accurate.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses recognizable section headings and simple, parsing-friendly formatting. However, its ATS coverage is weak because it contains very few relevant keywords from the advertisement. It does not mention Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, cloud infrastructure, systems architecture, system design, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, security, observability, reliability, stakeholder engagement or infrastructure operation. These terms must not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience, but the CV should describe any truthful relevant experience already held. The current document would have a low-to-moderate AI screening probability because the role-specific evidence is sparse. The all-caps name and basic heading structure are acceptable, but completing all placeholders and adding standard sections such as Technical Skills and Education/Certifications only where supported would improve parsing and credibility.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest demonstrated alignment is technical leadership, mentoring backend engineers into SRE roles, platform-team experience, service-mesh evaluation and clear communication through a technical talk. The CV does not demonstrate the core infrastructure and connectivity scope of the position: hands-on cloud design and operation, Terraform/Terragrunt, systems architecture, networking, mTLS/SSL/TLS, practical security, production ownership or stakeholder work with external engineering teams. The candidate notes explicitly state that GCP and Azure are absent, while AWS is not mentioned, so AWS is not demonstrated. There is also no candidate evidence of IoT, automotive or remote-device integration, Linux, virtual machines or JVM/full-stack development. These are capability gaps or unsupported areas in the available candidate material, not defects that can be solved by wording alone. The speaking example supports communication, but analytical thinking and stakeholder engagement are not yet evidenced.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the header, replace “NADIA [SURNAME]”, “[EMAIL]” and “[PHONE]” with the candidate’s actual professional name and contact details before submission. Replace “[EMPLOYER]” and “[DATES]” in the Experience section with the actual employer name and employment dates. Do not submit the CV with placeholders.

CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, make the leadership scope more explicit and use the accurate distinction already supported by the candidate’s notes. For example: “Senior Platform Engineer and technical lead for a platform team, with experience mentoring backend engineers into SRE roles and evaluating service-mesh technologies. Technical leadership is not a line-management responsibility.”

CRITICAL — Add a “TECHNICAL SKILLS” section immediately below the Professional Summary, but include only technologies and practices confirmed in the candidate’s original material. At minimum, list “Istio,” “Linkerd,” “Backstage Catalog,” “SRE,” “platform engineering” and “technical leadership.” Do not add Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, GCP, Azure, mTLS, SSL/TLS, networking, Linux, virtual machines or security unless the candidate confirms actual experience with them.

CRITICAL — Expand the Senior Platform Engineer entry with separate bullets that make the existing evidence more searchable and precise. For example, retain or revise the current bullets to include: “Technical lead for the platform team, with responsibility for technical direction and no line-management responsibility”; “Mentored three backend engineers transitioning into SRE roles”; and “Evaluated Istio and Linkerd in 2023 as service-mesh options; neither was adopted or operated in production.” This preserves the important limitation and avoids implying production experience.

CRITICAL — Revise the Backstage bullet to prevent any suggestion that the candidate built plugins. Use: “Used the Backstage catalog; plugins were developed by another team.” This is more concise and accurately reflects the candidate’s contribution.

MINOR — In the Speaking section, add the event type and preserve the exact talk title for stronger communication evidence: “Speaker, UK DevOps meetup, 2024 — ‘SLOs that product managers care about.’”

MINOR — Add an “ADDITIONAL INFORMATION” or “CERTIFICATIONS” section only if there is other truthful, relevant candidate information available. Do not list the CKAD because the candidate stated that it expired in 2025 and was not renewed.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The CV contains unresolved placeholders for the candidate’s name, contact details, employer and dates, making it appear incomplete and unsuitable for submission. Fix: replace every placeholder in the header and Professional Experience section with the actual information.
2. The CV does not provide evidence for most must-have technical requirements, including hands-on cloud infrastructure design and operation, Terraform/Terragrunt, systems architecture, networking, mTLS/SSL/TLS and practical security. These are alignment gaps in the available candidate material rather than claims that should be invented. Fix: only add verified experience if the candidate confirms it; otherwise leave these areas out rather than implying competence.
3. The Backstage statement could be misread as plugin-development experience unless its limitation is retained. Fix: change it to “Used the Backstage catalog; plugins were developed by another team.”

content:
NADIA

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Platform Engineer and technical lead for a platform team, with experience mentoring backend engineers into SRE roles and evaluating service-mesh technologies. Technical leadership does not include line-management responsibility.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Istio | Linkerd | Backstage Catalog | SRE | Platform engineering | Technical leadership

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer
- Serve as technical lead for the platform team, without line-management responsibility.
- Mentored three backend engineers transitioning into SRE roles.
- Evaluated Istio and Linkerd in 2023 as service-mesh options; neither was adopted or operated in production.
- Used the Backstage catalog; plugins were developed by another team.

SPEAKING
Speaker, UK DevOps meetup, 2024 — “SLOs that product managers care about”

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is concise, readable and unusually careful about distinguishing direct experience from evaluation or exposure. The Senior Platform Engineer title, technical-lead role, mentoring outcome, service-mesh evaluation and speaking engagement are clearly presented. However, it is not yet a complete CV: it lacks employer and employment dates, contact details, a fuller professional history, measurable platform outcomes and evidence of scope. The summary is also overly defensive, particularly the sentence about line management, and the skills section presents Istio, Linkerd and Backstage without their important usage limitations. Because the original candidate information is very limited, the document should not be expanded with unsupported technologies or responsibilities.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The simple headings, plain text formatting and standard section names are ATS-friendly, with no tables, graphics or complex layout. Relevant terms such as platform engineering, SRE, technical leadership, Istio, Linkerd and Backstage are present. ATS and AI screening probability for this particular role is currently low to moderate because the CV contains no evidence or keywords for Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS or another cloud, cloud infrastructure operation, systems architecture, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, security, stakeholder engagement or observability. These are not automatically document defects where the original candidate information provides no supporting evidence, and unsupported terms must not be added. The service-mesh and Backstage qualifications should be placed directly beside the technologies to prevent misleading keyword interpretation.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with technical leadership, platform engineering, SRE mentoring, clear communication and evaluating service-mesh technologies. The meetup presentation supports communication, and leading a platform team supports the technical-leadership requirement. The CV does not establish the role's core delivery scope: hands-on cloud infrastructure design and operation, Terraform/Terragrunt, systems architecture, networking with mTLS and SSL/TLS, practical security, stakeholder engagement, or production operation of a service mesh. AWS is not supported; the notes explicitly state no GCP or Azure. IoT, automotive or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, Linux and virtual machines are also not evidenced. The document therefore shows some relevant platform leadership but does not currently demonstrate a convincing match for a fleet-connectivity infrastructure contractor role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH IMPACT
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the defensive wording "Technical leadership does not include line-management responsibility" with a positive, precise formulation such as: "Provides technical direction for a platform team without formal line-management responsibility." Keep the distinction clear, but present it as scope rather than a disclaimer.
2. In the Technical Skills section, qualify technologies according to the experience actually documented. For example, change the list to: "Platform engineering | SRE | Technical leadership | Service-mesh evaluation: Istio, Linkerd | Backstage Catalog usage | Engineering mentoring." Do not list Istio or Linkerd as unqualified production skills, and do not imply that the candidate developed Backstage plugins.
3. In the Professional Experience section, add the employer name and employment dates if they exist in the candidate's records. The current entry contains only a job title, which weakens chronology, ATS parsing and credibility. Do not invent an employer or dates.
4. In the Professional Experience section, make the leadership and mentoring bullets more outcome-oriented without adding unsupported metrics. For example, change "Mentored three backend engineers transitioning into SRE roles" to "Mentored three backend engineers through their transition into SRE roles, supporting development of platform reliability capability." Only retain the added outcome if it is accurate.
5. In the Professional Experience section, clarify the limits of the service-mesh work in one compact bullet: "Evaluated Istio and Linkerd in 2023 as service-mesh options; neither was adopted or operated in production." This is already truthful; retain the explicit production limitation while ensuring the technologies are not interpreted as production-operational experience.
6. In the Speaking section, use a conventional ATS-readable entry format: "Speaker, UK DevOps Meetup | 2024 | ‘SLOs That Product Managers Care About’." Keep this as evidence of communication and the existing SLO subject; do not claim conference scale or audience size.

MINOR
7. Add a Contact section containing the candidate's actual email, phone, LinkedIn and/or portfolio details if available. Do not add placeholder or invented contact information.
8. If the candidate has documented examples of platform outcomes, architecture decisions, production operation, stakeholder engagement or reliability improvements that are not included in the supplied material, add them as specific bullets under the relevant role. Do not add Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS, SSL/TLS, security, Linux, virtual machines or fleet/IoT experience unless the candidate can substantiate it.
critique.critical_issues: No clear hallucinated skills or experiences were detected. The CV accurately states that Istio and Linkerd were evaluated but not adopted or operated in production, that Backstage plugins were developed by another team, and that the technical-lead role has no line-management responsibility. The main critical document issue is that the skills section can cause ATS or recruiter misinterpretation by listing technologies without their usage qualifiers; this must be corrected as specified in improvement instruction 2. The missing employer/dates and contact details are also significant completeness issues, but they must be supplied only if they exist in the candidate's records.
